content.title: Share State by Lifting It Up
content.hook: Imagine two panels where only one can be active at a time.
content.context:
A tempting design is:

```text
Panel A owns active state
Panel B owns active state
```

But then each panel can think it is active at the same time.

When multiple components need to stay synchronized, React's standard move is to lift the shared state to their closest common parent and pass the state and actions down through props.
goals: Move shared state to the closest common parent and pass values and event handlers through props.

content.question:
```text
Accordion
├── Panel A
└── Panel B
```

Both panels need the same `activeIndex` information.

Where should it live?

feedback.correct: `Accordion` is the closest common parent, so it is the natural owner of the shared state.
feedback.incorrect: `Accordion` is the closest common parent, so it is the natural owner of the shared state.

content.title: Build the data flow

activities.title: The child does not need to own the state

content.title: The child does not need to own the state
content.text:
A child can say:

```jsx
<button onClick={onShow}>Show</button>
```

The child does not need to know where the state lives.

That separation keeps the data path explicit.

content.question: If Panel A calls its `onShow`, what changes?

options.text: Only Panel A's private memory changes.
The parent updates `activeIndex`, then both panels can render from the new shared value.
Both panels create their own new state.

feedback.correct: One owner updates the source of truth. Both children receive the resulting state through props.
feedback.incorrect: One owner updates the source of truth. Both children receive the resulting state through props.

content.title: Practice: lift the state
content.text:
You are given two child components that each have:

```jsx
const [active, setActive] = useState(false);
```

Your task is to remove that duplicated state and move one shared value into the parent.

**Target design:**

```text
Parent owns selected item
        ↓ values
Children render from props
        ↑ callbacks
Children request changes
```

content.question: When two components must stay synchronized, what is the usual first move?

options.text: Put the shared state in their closest common parent.
Manually edit the DOM in each child.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. Put the shared state in their closest common parent.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. Put the shared state in their closest common parent.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Shared state usually has one owner; other components receive data and send requests through props/callbacks.
**Senior habit:** When two components disagree about the same fact, look for duplicated state before adding more logic.
nextSteps: Move one piece of duplicated child state into the parent and explain why one source of truth is easier to reason about.
